subject: physics
content: A particle of mass 4M at rest disintegrates into two particles of mass M and 3M respectively having non zero velocities. The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of particle of mass M to that of mass 3M will be :

options.content: 1 : <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.251ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="3.061ex" height="2.398ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -949 1353 1060" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="msqrt"><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(0,89)"><use data-c="221A" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-221A"></use></g><g transform="translate(853,0)"><g data-mml-node="mn"><use data-c="33" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-33"></use></g></g><rect width="500" height="60" x="853" y="829"></rect></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>

explanation:
both the particles will move with momentum same in magnitude & opposite in direction.

So De-Broglie wavelength of both will be same i.e. ratio 1 : 1
